name: application-form-autosave-banner
title: Form Autosave Banner
description: Form status bar: an amber 'unsaved changes' state with Discard/Save actions, or a neutral 'all saved' confirmation with a relative timestamp.
useWhen: A long-lived edit form (settings, profile, document) needs to communicate save state and let users act on unsaved changes.
You want a single banner that carries Discard/Save actions when there's something to resolve, not just a passive status icon.
Pairing with a sticky page layout so the banner stays visible while scrolling a long form.
avoidWhen: You only need a small inline status glyph (e.g. next to a field) with no discard/save actions — use a bare save-status indicator instead.
The form autosaves silently with no user-facing discard option — a passive 'Saved' toast is enough.
responsiveBehavior: The unsaved-state banner keeps its message and actions on one row down to narrow widths since both are short; wrap only if the container is narrower than the action buttons require.
accessibility: The unsaved-changes state is conveyed by a colored dot, background tint, and — critically — text ("You have unsaved changes"), not tint alone.
Discard and Save are both real, clearly labeled buttons so their destructive vs. constructive intent is legible independent of color.
The saved state's relative timestamp is plain text, giving a concrete reference point rather than relying on a vague icon alone.

variants.title: Form Autosave Banner
variants.description: An amber unsaved-changes bar with Discard and Save changes buttons, and a neutral all-saved confirmation bar with a checkmark and relative timestamp.
accessibility: Save/Discard button text conveys intent independent of their amber vs. neutral background colors.

variants.title: Form Autosave Banner (Dark)
variants.description: The same unsaved and saved states adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Amber tint and button contrast remain legible against the dark surface in both states.
